title: Kaizad Bharucha and a leading banker with rival seen as contenders for HDFC Bank's top job- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: 15                          Quick, easy & completely paperless. External candidate is said to be a private banker. Sources say RBI approval for CEO is likely by month-end or earlier   September 12, 2026 / 22:36 IST             HDFC Bank’s board on September 12 submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for appointment as the bank’s next managing director and chief executive officer, the bank said in an exchange filing. While the identities of the candidates have not been revealed by the bank, Kaizad Bharucha, HDFC Bank’s deputy managing director and one of its longest-serving senior executives, is understood to have emerged as the internal contender in the succession race. The other name recommended by the board is said to be an experienced banker with a private bank. Moneycontrol had earlier reported that  Bharucha was perceived to be the front-runner among senior executives, while the board was also sounding out bankers outside the bank. The development comes days after current MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan informed the board on August 29 that he would not seek reappointment for a third term. His second term ends on October 26, 2026, following which he will retire from the bank. A source privy to internal board discussions said the RBI approval for MD & CEO should come through by end of September or even earlier. "With the names in the order of preference having been communicated to the RBI today, the wait should not be too long," he added. Bharucha emerges as key internal name Bharucha has been with HDFC Bank since 1995 and is currently its deputy managing director. He has been the bank’s longest-serving executive board member, having first joined the board as an executive director in 2014. However, his candidature comes with a regulatory consideration. RBI rules cap the tenure of whole-time directors at private sector banks at 15 years. Since Bharucha became an executive director in 2014, his tenure on the board would run until 2029. This means that, unless the RBI provides an exemption or changes the applicable rule, he could potentially have only about three years as CEO. Some brokerages such as Nomura and Motilal Oswal have argued that an internal appointment would provide a smoother transition, while an external candidate could offer a longer leadership runway and a more pronounced strategic reset. External candidate still possible Moneycontrol reported that HDFC Bank chairman Rajiv Kumar, along with members of the GNRC, had begun reaching out to bankers outside the bank. "The board took a view that the CEO candidate should be an active banker with a leading private bank. This decision was taken after feedback from multiple stakeholders including investors," said a person aware of the shortlisting process. The external pool of candidates reported by Moneycontrol include Tata Capital’s Rajiv Sabharwal, ICICI Prudential Life’s Anup Bagchi and Aditya Birla Capital’s Vishaka Mulye, while news reports suggest Citibank's India CEO K Balasubramanian and HSBC's Hitender Dave could also to have been in the fray. Certain research reports also named Axis Bank's CEO Amitabh Chaudhry as a potential candidate. CNBC-TV18 had reported that Dinesh Khara, former chairman of State Bank of India, is also being considered for the position. The external candidate, according to a source involved in the process was assessed on the ability to strengthen governance and bring in second rung leaders from outside into HDFC Bank. “HDFC Bank is highly process driven and it would not be challenging for an outsider to quickly adapt to the bank,” a senior executive had told Moneycontrol. In August, ahead of Jagdishan's decision to step down as MD & CEO, Moneycontrol reported that Kumar had met RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra to update the regulator on where the board stood on the CEO succession issue. New whole-time director positions According to the filing dated September 12, the board has also moved to strengthen its executive structure alongside the CEO search. It has recommended the reappointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director, designated as executive director, from November 23, 2026 to November 22, 2027. The board has also recommended the appointment of Jimmy Tata as a whole-time director, designated as executive director, for three years, subject to RBI approval. In addition, HDFC Bank has approved the creation of one more whole-time director position, taking the total number of whole-time directors on the board to four, apart from the MD & CEO. The bank said the additional position is intended to provide sharper synergy and oversight, including across subsidiaries, as well as create a larger pipeline for succession planning. The position will be filled in consultation with the incoming MD & CEO after the new chief takes charge.                        Discover the latest  Business News ,  Sensex , and  Nifty  updates. September 12, 2026 / 22:36 IST

HDFC Bank’s board on September 12 submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for appointment as the bank’s next managing director and chief executive officer, the bank said in an exchange filing.

While the identities of the candidates have not been revealed by the bank, Kaizad Bharucha, HDFC Bank’s deputy managing director and one of its longest-serving senior executives, is understood to have emerged as the internal contender in the succession race.

The other name recommended by the board is said to be an experienced banker with a private bank.

Moneycontrol had earlier reported that Bharucha was perceived to be the front-runner among senior executives, while the board was also sounding out bankers outside the bank.

The development comes days after current MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan informed the board on August 29 that he would not seek reappointment for a third term. His second term ends on October 26, 2026, following which he will retire from the bank.

A source privy to internal board discussions said the RBI approval for MD & CEO should come through by end of September or even earlier. "With the names in the order of preference having been communicated to the RBI today, the wait should not be too long," he added.

Bharucha emerges as key internal name

Bharucha has been with HDFC Bank since 1995 and is currently its deputy managing director. He has been the bank’s longest-serving executive board member, having first joined the board as an executive director in 2014.

However, his candidature comes with a regulatory consideration. RBI rules cap the tenure of whole-time directors at private sector banks at 15 years. Since Bharucha became an executive director in 2014, his tenure on the board would run until 2029. This means that, unless the RBI provides an exemption or changes the applicable rule, he could potentially have only about three years as CEO.

Some brokerages such as Nomura and Motilal Oswal have argued that an internal appointment would provide a smoother transition, while an external candidate could offer a longer leadership runway and a more pronounced strategic reset.

External candidate still possible

Moneycontrol reported that HDFC Bank chairman Rajiv Kumar, along with members of the GNRC, had begun reaching out to bankers outside the bank.

"The board took a view that the CEO candidate should be an active banker with a leading private bank. This decision was taken after feedback from multiple stakeholders including investors," said a person aware of the shortlisting process.

The external pool of candidates reported by Moneycontrol include Tata Capital’s Rajiv Sabharwal, ICICI Prudential Life’s Anup Bagchi and Aditya Birla Capital’s Vishaka Mulye, while news reports suggest Citibank's India CEO K Balasubramanian and HSBC's Hitender Dave could also to have been in the fray. Certain research reports also named Axis Bank's CEO Amitabh Chaudhry as a potential candidate.

CNBC-TV18 had reported that Dinesh Khara, former chairman of State Bank of India, is also being considered for the position.

The external candidate, according to a source involved in the process was assessed on the ability to strengthen governance and bring in second rung leaders from outside into HDFC Bank. “HDFC Bank is highly process driven and it would not be challenging for an outsider to quickly adapt to the bank,” a senior executive had told Moneycontrol.

In August, ahead of Jagdishan's decision to step down as MD & CEO, Moneycontrol reported that Kumar had met RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra to update the regulator on where the board stood on the CEO succession issue.

New whole-time director positions

According to the filing dated September 12, the board has also moved to strengthen its executive structure alongside the CEO search.

It has recommended the reappointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director, designated as executive director, from November 23, 2026 to November 22, 2027.

The board has also recommended the appointment of Jimmy Tata as a whole-time director, designated as executive director, for three years, subject to RBI approval.

In addition, HDFC Bank has approved the creation of one more whole-time director position, taking the total number of whole-time directors on the board to four, apart from the MD & CEO.

The bank said the additional position is intended to provide sharper synergy and oversight, including across subsidiaries, as well as create a larger pipeline for succession planning. The position will be filled in consultation with the incoming MD & CEO after the new chief takes charge.
